note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Cough.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports that cough started approximately one week ago. He has been bringing up yellow sputum and has not been feeling well over the last two days. He states he feels warm but has not taken his temperature. He denies chills but reports feeling achy at times. He denies shortness of breath. He reports congestion with drainage down his throat and some pressure in his sinuses. He reports no one else in his household is sick. He works as a teacher. Additionally, patient reports that earlier today while coughing, he coughed a couple of times and twisted his right knee after falling down approximately four to five stairs. Injury occurred this morning. He is able to walk but has a slight limp. Pain is mostly on the inside of the knee. He reports he can bend and straighten the knee and does not feel like it will give out. He has been taking over-the-counter Dayquil for cough and cold symptoms with minimal relief.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies fever (has not taken temperature but feels warm). Denies chills. Reports feeling achy at times. Denies shortness of breath. Reports congestion with drainage down throat and pressure in sinuses. Reports right knee pain from fall earlier today.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension. Diabetes.

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 mg daily. Metformin 1000 mg twice daily. Over-the-counter Dayquil for cough and cold.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is a teacher. Not a sports fan. Age 74. Married. Does not watch salt intake. Does not monitor blood sugar intake.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Temperature 98.4°F, Blood Pressure 125/62, Heart Rate 80s, Oxygen saturation 97% on room air.
Facial Exam: Pain to palpation of bilateral maxillary sinuses under the eyes.
Nasal Exam: Erythema and edema of nasal turbinates bilaterally with associated yellow discharge.
Throat Exam: Uvula midline. No erythema, edema, or exudate in peritonsillar space.
Neck Exam: Bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy.
Lung Exam: Coarse rhonchi present bilaterally that clears with cough.
Heart Exam: Regular rate and rhythm. No murmur appreciated.
Right Knee Exam: Pain to palpation on right knee. Decreased flexion and extension of right knee. Ecchymosis to right medial knee. No evidence of effusion.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Viral syndrome with mild bronchitis: Supportive care. Continue over-the-counter medications. Prescribe guaifenesin 600 mg twice daily to help clear phlegm. No antibiotics at this time. Patient to call if symptoms worsen; will consider chest x-ray at that time to rule out pneumonia.
2. Right medial collateral ligament strain: Prescribe meloxicam 15 mg once daily. Refer to physical therapy. Order right knee x-ray to rule out bone injury.
3. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Order lipid panel.
4. Diabetes: Order hemoglobin A1c. Continue metformin. Patient to monitor sugar intake and report blood sugars through patient portal.
